paragraphs: Except where the context suggests otherwise, references in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to "EFC," "we," "us," and "our" refer to Ellington Financial Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, including Ellington Financial Operating Partnership LLC, our operating partnership subsidiary, which we refer to as our "Operating Partnership." References in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to (1) "common shares" refer to shares of our common stock, $0.001 par value per share and (2) "common stockholders" refer to holders of shares of our common stock. We conduct all of our operations and business activities through our Operating Partnership. Our "Manager" refers to Ellington Financial Management LLC, our external manager, "Ellington" refers to Ellington Management Group, L.L.C. and its affiliated investment advisory firms, including our Manager, and "Manager Group" refers collectively to officers and directors of EFC, and partners and affiliates of Ellington (including families and family trusts of the foregoing). In certain instances, references to our Manager and services to be provided to us by our Manager may also include services provided by Ellington and its other affiliates from time to time.

When used in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, in future filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, or the "SEC," or in press releases or other written or oral communications, statements which are not historical in nature, including those containing words such as "believe," "expect," "anticipate," "estimate," "project," "plan," "continue," "intend," "should," "would," "could," "goal," "objective," "will," "may," "seek," or similar expressions or their negative forms or references to strategy, plans or intentions, are intended to identify "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or the "Securities Act," and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or the "Exchange Act," and, as such, may involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and assumptions.

Forward-looking statements are based on our beliefs, assumptions, and expectations of our future operations, business strategies, performance, financial condition, liquidity and prospects, taking into account information currently available to us. These beliefs, assumptions, and expectations are subject to risks and uncertainties and can change as a result of many possible events or factors, not all of which are known to us. If a change occurs, our business, financial condition, liquidity, results of operations and strategies may vary materially from those expressed or implied in our forward-looking statements. The following factors are examples of those that could cause actual results to vary from our forward-looking statements: changes in interest rates and the market value of our securities or our investments; market volatility; changes in the prepayment rates on the mortgage loans owned by us, or underlying the securities owned by us; increased rates of default and/or decreased recovery rates on our assets; our ability to borrow to finance our assets and the available terms for such borrowings; changes in government regulations affecting our business; our ability to maintain our exclusion from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the "Investment Company Act"); our ability to maintain our qualification as a real estate investment trust ("REIT"); and risks associated with investing in real estate assets, including changes in business conditions and the general economy such as changes to fiscal or monetary policy, heightened inflation, slower growth or recession, and currency fluctuations. These and other risks, uncertainties and factors, including the risk factors described under Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected or implied in any forward-looking statements we make. All forward-looking statements speak only as of the date on which they are made. New risks and uncertainties arise over time, and it is not possible to predict those events or how they may affect us. Except as required by law, we are not obligated to, and do not intend to, update or revise any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise.

We are a Delaware corporation operating as a real estate investment trust ("REIT") and are listed on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the symbol "EFC." We were formed in July 2007 and became a publicly traded company following our initial public offering in October 2010.

We employ a credit-focused investment strategy and manage a diversified portfolio totaling approximately $4.9 billion as of December 31, 2025. Our primary objective is to generate attractive risk-adjusted total returns for our stockholders by making investments that we believe appropriately compensate us for the risks we assume. Our strategic focus is on residential and commercial mortgage loan investments, sourced through a diverse array of loan origination channels, including certain affiliated loan originators. We opportunistically invest in both loans and securities. Through Longbridge Financial LLC ("Longbridge"), a wholly-owned and consolidated subsidiary of our Operating Partnership, we are also in the business of originating, servicing, and investing in reverse mortgage loans.

We are externally managed and advised by our Manager, an affiliate of Ellington, which is responsible for administering our business activities and day-to-day operations. Pursuant to a services agreement between our Manager and Ellington, our Manager relies on Ellington's personnel and infrastructure to support our operations. Most members of our executive management team also serve as officers of our Manager and Ellington.

We intend to maintain our qualification to be taxed as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"). Provided that we maintain our qualification as a REIT, we generally will not be subject to U.S. federal, state, and local income tax on our REIT taxable income that is currently distributed to our stockholders, so long as we distribute at least 90% of our REIT taxable income (excluding net capital gains) to our stockholders by prescribed dates and comply with various other requirements. Any taxes paid by a taxable REIT subsidiary ("TRS") will reduce the cash available for distribution to our stockholders.

We acquire and manage mortgage-related, consumer-related, corporate-related, and other financial assets, including those listed below. For a more detailed description of our targeted asset classes, see Part II, Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Our Targeted Asset Classes."

•Agency RMBS, including (i) whole pool pass-through certificates; (ii) partial pool pass-through certificates; and (iii) agency collateralized mortgage obligations ("CMOs"), including interest only securities ("IOs"), principal only securities ("POs"), and inverse interest only securities ("IIOs");
•CMBS and Commercial Mortgage Loans, including (i) CMBS; (ii) CLOs backed by commercial mortgage loans ("CRE CLOs"); and (iii) commercial mortgage loans and other commercial real estate debt;

•Consumer Loans and ABS, including (i) consumer loans; (ii) ABS backed by consumer loans; (iii) ABS backed by Small Business Administration ("SBA") loans, including IOs backed by SBA loans; and (iv) retained tranches from securitizations to which we have contributed assets;
•Corporate CLOs, including (i) corporate CLO debt and equity tranches; and (ii) investments in CLO loan accumulation facilities;

•Mortgage-Related Derivatives, including (i) To-Be-Announced mortgage pass-through certificates ("TBAs"); (ii) credit default swaps ("CDS") on individual RMBS, on the CMBX and other mortgage-related indices; and (iii) other mortgage-related derivatives;

•Non-Agency RMBS, including: (i) RMBS backed by prime jumbo, Alt-A, non-QM, manufactured housing, and subprime mortgages; (ii) RMBS backed by fixed rate mortgages, Adjustable rate mortgages ("ARMs"), Option-ARMs, and Hybrid ARMs; (iii) RMBS backed by mortgages on single-family-rental properties; (iv) RMBS backed by first-lien and second-lien mortgages; (v) RMBS backed by performing and non-performing mortgages; (vi) investment grade and non-investment grade securities; (vii) senior and subordinated securities; (viii) IOs, POs, IIOs, and inverse floaters; (ix) collateralized debt obligations ("CDOs"); (x) RMBS backed by European residential mortgages ("European RMBS"); (xi) retained tranches from securitizations in which we have participated; and (xi) credit risk transfer securities ("CRTs");

Difficult conditions in the mortgage and residential and commercial real estate markets as well as general market concerns may adversely affect the value of the assets in which we invest.
Mortgage loan modification programs and future legislative action may adversely affect the value of, and the returns on, our assets.

Less stringent underwriting guidelines and the resultant potential for delinquencies or defaults on certain mortgage loans could lead to losses on many of the non-Agency RMBS and European RMBS that we hold.
We have invested and may in the future invest in securities in the CRT sector that are subject to mortgage credit risk.
Prepayment rates can change, adversely affecting the performance of our assets.

paragraphs: •Difficult conditions in the mortgage, real estate, and financial markets, including economic downturns, inflation, elevated interest rates, declining property values, and tightening credit availability, could adversely affect the value of our investments and our financial performance. Market volatility and economic instability may lead to increased borrower delinquencies, declining liquidity, and reduced availability of financing, all of which could negatively impact our returns.

•Regulatory changes affecting Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae could materially impact mortgage market liquidity and valuations. Any changes in their government backing, capital requirements, or underwriting guidelines could disrupt the market for Agency RMBS and impact the pricing of our mortgage-related assets. Additionally, federal or state-level government intervention, such as mortgage modification programs, foreclosure moratoriums, or new regulations affecting loan servicing, could reduce the value of our assets or delay our ability to recover on defaulted loans.

•We are exposed to significant credit risks through our investments in residential and commercial mortgage loans, MBS, CRTs, and CLOs. Borrower delinquencies, defaults, and declining collateral values may result in losses, particularly in residential and commercial mortgage loans, non-Agency RMBS, CRTs, and loans with lower underwriting standards. Second-lien loans are especially vulnerable, as they are subordinate to first-lien loans and may suffer complete loss in foreclosure scenarios.

•Certain mortgage-backed securities and whole loans we acquire may have been underwritten with less stringent credit standards. Loans originated with reduced documentation requirements, high loan-to-value ratios, or weak borrower credit profiles pose a higher risk of delinquency and default, which may reduce the performance of non-Agency RMBS and CRT securities in which we invest. Additionally, sellers of mortgage loans we acquire may be unable or unwilling to repurchase defective loans, resulting in additional losses.

•We depend on service providers, including mortgage servicers, for a variety of services related to many of our assets, including MSRs, RMBS, CRTs, securitizations, and loan pools. If servicers fail to perform effectively, including loss mitigation efforts or foreclosure processing, we may experience increased delinquencies, reduced cash flows, and reputational harm. We may also be affected by deficiencies in foreclosure practices by third parties, which could cause delays and additional legal risks.

•Interest rate mismatches between our assets and liabilities could negatively impact our net interest income, particularly in periods of rising interest rates. Additionally, certain assets, such as adjustable-rate mortgages and hybrid ARMs, are subject to interest rate caps that may limit our ability to pass on higher interest costs, reducing profitability.

paragraphs: Our primary objective is to generate attractive risk-adjusted total returns for our stockholders. We seek to attain this objective by utilizing an opportunistic strategy to make investments, without restriction as to ratings, structure, or position in the capital structure, that we believe compensate us appropriately for the risks associated with them rather than targeting a specific yield. At any particular point in time, depending on how we perceive the market's pricing of risk both generally and across sectors, we may favor higher-risk assets or we may favor lower-risk assets, or a combination of the two, in the interests of portfolio diversification or other considerations.

We conduct all of our operations and business activities through the Operating Partnership. As of December 31, 2025, we had an ownership interest of approximately 99.1% in the Operating Partnership. The remaining ownership interest of approximately 0.9% in the Operating Partnership represents the interests in the Operating Partnership that are owned by an affiliate of our Manager, our current and certain former directors, and certain current and former Ellington employees and their related parties, and is reflected in our financial statements as a non-controlling interest. We are externally managed and advised by our Manager, an affiliate of Ellington. Ellington is a registered investment adviser with a 31-year history of investing in the Agency and credit markets.

We have elected to be taxed as a REIT under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"). Provided that we maintain our qualification as a REIT, we generally will not be subject to U.S. federal, state, and local income tax on our REIT taxable income that is currently distributed to our stockholders. Any taxes paid by a domestic taxable REIT subsidiary ("TRS") will reduce the cash available for distribution to our stockholders. REITs are subject to a number of organizational and operational requirements, including a requirement that they currently distribute at least 90% of their annual REIT taxable income excluding net capital gains.

On December 14, 2023, we completed a merger between Arlington Asset Investment Corp., a Virginia corporation ("Arlington"), and our subsidiary EF Merger Sub Inc., a Virginia corporation (such transaction, the "Arlington Merger").

We have two reportable segments, the Investment Portfolio Segment and the Longbridge Segment. In our Investment Portfolio Segment, we invest in a diverse array of financial assets, including residential and commercial mortgage loans; residential mortgage-backed securities ("RMBS"), including RMBS for which the principal and interest payments are guaranteed by a U.S. government agency or a U.S. government-sponsored entity ("Agency RMBS"); commercial mortgage-backed securities ("CMBS"); consumer loans and asset-backed securities ("ABS") including ABS backed by consumer loans; investments referencing mortgage servicing rights on traditional forward mortgage loans ("Forward MSR-related investments"); collateralized loan obligations ("CLOs"); non-mortgage- and mortgage-related derivatives; debt and equity investments in loan origination companies; and other strategic investments. We refer to the portion of our investment portfolio excluding Agency RMBS as our credit portfolio.

Our Longbridge Segment is focused on the origination and servicing of, and investment in, reverse mortgage loans, including associated financial assets, financing, hedging, and allocated expenses. Longbridge Financial, LLC ("Longbridge") originates home equity conversion mortgage loans ("HECM loans"), which are insured by the Federal Housing Administration ("FHA"), and non-FHA-insured reverse mortgage loans, which we refer to as "proprietary reverse mortgage loans." HECM loans are generally eligible for securitization into HECM-backed MBS ("HMBS"), which are guaranteed by the Government National Mortgage Association ("GNMA").

The strategies that we employ are intended to capitalize on opportunities in the current market environment. Subject to maintaining our qualification as a REIT and our exclusion from registration as an investment company under the Investment Company Act, we intend to adjust our strategies to changing market conditions by shifting our asset allocations across various asset classes as credit and liquidity trends evolve over time. We believe that this flexibility, combined with Ellington's experience, will help us generate more consistent returns on our capital throughout changing market cycles. Additionally, subject to maintaining our qualification as a REIT, we opportunistically hedge our credit risk, interest rate risk, yield spread risk, and foreign currency risk; however, at any point in time we may choose not to hedge all or a portion of these risks, and we will generally not hedge those risks that we believe are appropriate for us to take at such time, or that we believe would be impractical or prohibitively expensive to hedge. For more information on our targeted assets, see "—Our Targeted Asset Classes" below.

paragraphs: 除非上下文另有說明，本年度報告表10-K中提及的「EFC」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們」均指Ellington Financial Inc.及其合併子公司，包括Ellington Financial Operating Partnership LLC，我們的營運合夥企業子公司，我們稱之為「營運合夥企業」。本年度報告表10-K中提及的(1)「普通股」指我們普通股，每股面值0.001美元，以及(2)「普通股股東」指持有我們普通股的股東。我們透過營運合夥企業進行所有營運及商業活動。我們的「管理人」指Ellington Financial Management LLC，我們的外部管理人，「Ellington」指Ellington Management Group, L.L.C.及其附屬投資顧問公司，包括我們的管理人，而「管理集團」則指EFC的董事及高階主管，以及Ellington的合夥人及附屬機構（包括其家族及家族信託）。在某些情況下，提及我們的管理人及管理人提供給我們的服務，也可能包括Ellington及其其他附屬機構偶爾提供的服務。

在本年度報告表10-K中，未來向證券交易委員會（「SEC」）提交的文件，或在新聞稿或其他書面或口頭溝通中使用時，任何非歷史性陳述，包括包含「相信」、「預期」、「預期」、「預估」、「預測」、「計畫」、「持續」、「意圖」、「應該」、「將」、「可能」、「追求」或類似詞彙或其否定形式，或提及策略、計畫或意圖的參考，旨在識別「前瞻性陳述」，根據1933年證券法（「證券法」）第27A條或1934年證券交易法（「證券交易法」）第21E條的定義，並可能涉及已知及未知的風險、不確定性及假設。

前瞻性陳述基於我們對未來營運、業務策略、表現、財務狀況、流動性及前景的信念、假設及預期，並考慮目前可得資訊。這些信念、假設及預期可能因許多可能事件或因素而改變，並非全部為我們所知。如果發生變化，我們的業務、財務狀況、流動性、營運結果及策略可能與前瞻性陳述中所表達或暗示的有重大差異。以下因素為可能導致實際結果與前瞻性陳述有所差異的範例：利率變動及我們證券或投資的市場價值變動；市場波動；我們持有的抵押貸款或相關證券的預付率變動；我們資產的違約率增加或回收率下降；我們借款以資金融通資產的能力及相關借款條件；影響我們業務的政府規範變動；我們維持根據1940年投資公司法（「投資公司法」）免於註冊的資格；我們維持符合實體投資信託（「REIT」）資格的能力；以及投資於不動產資產的風險，包括商業條件及總體經濟變動，如財政或貨幣政策變動、通貨膨脹升高、成長放緩或經濟衰退，以及貨幣兌換波動。這些及其他風險、不確定性及因素，包括本年度報告表10-K第1A項所描述的風險因素，可能導致我們的實際結果與前瞻性陳述中所預測或暗示的有重大差異。所有前瞻性陳述僅於其作出之日為準。隨時間推移，會產生新的風險及不確定性，且無法預測這些事件或它們如何影響我們。除非法律要求，我們不負有更新或修正任何前瞻性陳述的義務，也不打算更新或修正任何前瞻性陳述，無論因新資訊、未來事件或其他原因。
我們是一家特拉華州公司，以實體投資信託（「REIT」）形式運作，並在紐約證券交易所（「紐約證券交易所」）以符號「EFC」上市。我們於2007年7月成立，並在2010年10月首次公開發行後成為公開交易公司。

我們採用以信用為導向的投資策略，並管理總計約49億美元的多元化投資組合，截至2025年12月31日。我們的主要目標是透過我們認為能適度補償我們所承擔風險的投資，為股東產生有吸引力的風險調整後總回報。我們的戰略重點在於住宅及商業抵押貸款投資，這些投資來自多樣化的貸款發放渠道，包括某些附屬貸款發放機構。我們會機會性地投資於貸款及證券。透過Longbridge Financial LLC（「Longbridge」），我們的營運合夥企業全資及合併子公司，我們也從事反向抵押貸款的發放、服務及投資業務。
我們由外部管理及顧問機構管理，即我們的管理人，為Ellington的附屬機構，負責管理我們的業務活動及日常營運。根據我們的管理人與Ellington之間的服務協議，我們的管理人依賴Ellington的員工及基礎設施來支援我們的營運。我們的高階管理團隊大多數成員同時擔任我們管理人及Ellington的高階主管。
我們意圖維持根據1986年美國內政部稅收法（「稅收法」）第27A條規定，以REIT形式納稅的資格。只要我們維持REIT資格，我們通常不會就我們REIT應課稅收入（扣除淨資本利得）對美國聯邦、州及地方收入稅負擔，只要我們在規定日期前至少分派90%的REIT應課稅收入給股東，並符合其他相關要求。任何由應課稅REIT子公司（「TRS」）支付的稅款將減少可供分派給股東的現金。
我們取得並管理與抵押貸款、消費者貸款、企業貸款及其他金融資產相關的資產，包括以下所列資產。如需更詳細的資產類別描述，請參閱第二部分，第7項「管理層對財務狀況及營運結果的討論與分析—我們的目標資產類別」。
•代理機構房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS），包括 (i) 完整池過戶證書；(ii) 部分池過戶證書；以及 (iii) 代理機構抵押貸款過戶證券（"CMOs"），包括利息過戶證券（"IOs"）、本金過戶證券（"POs"）以及反向利息過戶證券（"IIOs"）；
•商業抵押貸款支持證券（CMBS）及商業抵押貸款，包括 (i) CMBS；(ii) 由商業抵押貸款支持的信貸貸款過戶證券（"CRE CLOs"）；以及 (iii) 商業抵押貸款及其他商業不動產貸款；
•消費者貸款及過戶證券（ABS），包括 (i) 消費者貸款；(ii) 由消費者貸款支持的過戶證券；(iii) 由小企業管理局（"SBA"）貸款支持的過戶證券，包括由 SBA 貸款支持的利息過戶證券；以及 (iv) 我們已貢獻資產的過戶證券中保留的分層；
•企業信貸貸款過戶證券（Corporate CLOs），包括 (i) 企業信貸貸款過戶證券的債務及權益分層；以及 (ii) 投資於信貸貸款過戶證券貸款積累設施；
•房貸相關衍生工具，包括 (i) 尚未公告的房貸過戶證書（"TBAs"）；(ii) 個別 RMBS 的信用違約交換（"CDS"），在 CMBX 及其他房貸相關指數上；以及 (iii) 其他房貸相關衍生工具；

•非代理機構房貸支持證券（Non-Agency RMBS），包括：(i) 由優質大額、Alt-A、非合格房貸、製造住宅及次級房貸支持的 RMBS；(ii) 由固定利率房貸、可調利率房貸（"ARMs"）、選擇性 ARM 貸款及混合 ARM 貸款支持的 RMBS；(iii) 由單戶出租住宅房貸支持的 RMBS；(iv) 由首優先及次優先房貸支持的 RMBS；(v) 由表現良好及表現不佳房貸支持的 RMBS；(vi) 投資等級及非投資等級證券；(vii) 資產級及次級證券；(viii) 利息過戶證券、本金過戶證券、反向利息過戶證券及反向浮動證券；(ix) 抵押債務過戶證券（"CDOs"）；(x) 由歐洲住宅房貸支持的 RMBS（"European RMBS"）；(xi) 我們參與的過戶證券中保留的分層；以及 (xi) 信用風險轉移證券（"CRTs"）；

paragraphs: 本公司主要目標為為股東產生具吸引力的風險調整後總回報。我們透過採用機會主義策略進行投資，不設限於評級、結構或資本結構中的位置，以我們認為能適當補償與這些投資相關風險的方式進行，而非追求特定殖利率。在任何特定時間點，根據我們對市場風險評價的看法，無論是整體或各個產業，我們可能傾向高風險資產，或低風險資產，或兩者結合，以實現投資組合分散風險或其他考量。

我們透過營運合夥企業進行所有營運與商業活動。截至2025年12月31日，本公司在營運合夥企業中擁有約99.1%的權益。營運合夥企業中約0.9%的權益為本公司管理公司之關聯公司、本公司現任及曾任董事、以及某些現任及曾任Ellington員工及其關聯公司所擁有，並在財務報表中列為非控制性權益。本公司由本公司管理公司進行外部管理與諮詢，而本公司管理公司為Ellington之關聯公司。Ellington為經美國證券交易委員會註冊之投資顧問，擁有31年於機構與信用市場進行投資之經驗。
本公司已選擇根據1986年美國內政部稅法（「稅法」）被課徵為REIT（不動產投資信託）。只要我們維持REIT資格，我們一般不會就目前分發給股東之REIT應課稅所得，課徵美國聯邦、州及地方所得稅。任何由美國國內應課稅REIT子公司（「TRS」）所支付之稅款，將減少可供分發給股東之現金。REIT需遵守許多組織與營運要求，包括必須分發至少90%之年度REIT應課稅所得（扣除淨資本利得）。
2023年12月14日，本公司完成Arlington Asset Investment Corp.（位於維吉尼亞州之公司，簡稱「Arlington」）與我們之子公司EF Merger Sub Inc.（位於維吉尼亞州之公司）之合併（此交易稱為「Arlington合併」）。

本公司有兩個應報告分部，為投資組合分部與Longbridge分部。在投資組合分部，我們投資於多樣化的金融資產，包括住宅與商業房貸貸款；住宅房貸-backed證券（「RMBS」），包括由美國政府機構或美國政府支持機構擔保之本金與利息支付之RMBS（「Agency RMBS」）；商業房貸-backed證券（「CMBS」）；消費者貸款與資產-backed證券（「ABS」），包括由消費者貸款支持之ABS；參考傳統前向房貸貸款之房貸服務權投資（「Forward MSR相關投資」）；擔保貸款義務（「CLOs」）；非房貸與房貸相關衍生性商品；貸款發行公司之債務與權益投資；以及其他戰略投資。我們將投資組閤中排除Agency RMBS之部分稱為信用組合。

Longbridge分部專注於反向房貸貸款之發行與服務，以及投資，包括相關金融資產、融資、避險與分攤費用。Longbridge Financial, LLC（簡稱「Longbridge」）發行居家權益轉換房貸貸款（「HECM貸款」），這些貸款由美國房屋管理局（「FHA」）承保，以及非FHA承保之反向房貸貸款，我們稱為「自有反向房貸貸款」。HECM貸款通常可資格被組合成HECM-backed MBS（「HMBS」），這些MBS由美國政府國家抵押貸款協會（「GNMA」）擔保。

我們所採用的策略旨在把握目前市場環境中的機會。在維持REIT資格與不被歸類為投資公司之條件下，我們有意根據市場條件的變化，調整策略，透過跨不同資產類別的資產配置，以應對信用與流動性趨勢的變化。我們認為這種靈活性，加上Ellington的經驗，將有助於我們在不同市場週期中產生更一致的資本回報。此外，在維持REIT資格之條件下，我們會機會主義地避險信用風險、利率風險、殖利率差距風險與外匯風險；然而，在任何時間點，我們可能選擇不避險全部或部分這些風險，且我們通常不會避險那些我們認為在當時適合我們承擔，或我們認為避險將不實際或過於昂貴的風險。如需更多關於我們目標資產之資訊，請參閱下方「—我們的目標資產類別」。

paragraphs: •房貸、不動產及金融市場的困難情況，包括經濟衰退、通貨膨脹、利率偏高、房地產價值下降以及信貸取得困難，可能不利於我們投資的價值與財務表現。市場波動與經濟不穩定可能導致借款人違約增加、流動性下降以及融資取得減少，所有這些都可能對我們的回報產生負面影響。
•影響房利美、房地美及吉利美（Ginnie Mae）的法規變動，可能對房貸市場的流動性與評價產生重大影響。他們政府背書、資本要求或承貸標準的任何變動，都可能幹擾機構RMBS市場，並影響我們房貸相關資產的定價。此外，聯邦或州政府的幹預，例如房貸修改計畫、 foreclosure停擺令或影響貸款服務的新法規，可能降低我們資產的價值或延遲我們對違約貸款的回收能力。
•我們透過投資住宅及商業房貸貸款、MBS、CRTs及CLOs，面臨顯著的信用風險。借款人違約、違約及擔保品價值下降，可能導致虧損，特別是在住宅及商業房貸貸款、非機構RMBS、CRTs及貸款承貸標準較低的情況下。第二順位貸款尤其脆弱，因為它們在第一順位貸款之下，可能在 foreclosure 情境中完全損失。
•我們取得的某些房貸-backed證券及整筆貸款，可能曾以較為寬鬆的信用標準進行承貸。以減少文件要求、高貸款對價值比率或借款人信用資料較弱的貸款，可能導致違約及違約風險增加，這可能降低我們投資的非機構RMBS及CRT證券的表現。此外，我們取得的房貸貸款賣方可能無法或不願回購有缺陷的貸款，導致額外虧損。
•我們依賴服務提供者，包括房貸服務機構，為我們許多資產提供多種服務，包括MSRs、RMBS、CRTs、證券化產品及貸款池。如果服務機構未能有效執行，包括減損措施或 foreclosure 處理，我們可能面臨違約增加、現金流減少及聲譽損害。我們也可能受到第三方 foreclosure 程序缺陷的影響，導致延誤及額外法律風險。
•我們資產與負債之間的利率不匹配，可能對我們的淨利息收入產生負面影響，尤其是在利率上升期間。此外，某些資產，例如浮動利率房貸及混合型ARM，受到利率上限的限制，可能限制我們轉嫁更高利率成本的能力，降低利潤率。
